Is Wat Plai Laem free? | Yes, Wat Plai Laem is free to enter; donations are welcome and fish food from the temple dispensers costs a few baht.
What are Wat Plai Laem's opening hours? | The grounds are open roughly 06:00–18:00 every day; the ordination hall keeps shorter hours, and the late-night times on some map listings are wrong.
Who is the 18-armed statue at Wat Plai Laem? | It is Guanyin (Chao Mae Kuan Im in Thai), the bodhisattva of compassion; the 18 arms each hold an object or make a gesture, symbolising the many ways she helps people.
How far is Wat Plai Laem from the Big Buddha? | About 1 km east, a 3-minute drive on Route 4171; the road has no pavement, so drive or take a Grab rather than walking.
What should I wear at Wat Plai Laem? | Cover shoulders and knees and take your shoes off before entering the ordination hall; bring a scarf or sarong in case wraps are not available.
Can I feed the fish at Wat Plai Laem? | Yes, feeding the catfish, carp and turtles counts as merit-making, but use only the food sold by the temple, never bread or snacks.
When was Wat Plai Laem built? | The complex was built between 2004 and 2009, which makes it one of the newest major temples on Koh Samui.
Who is the laughing Buddha at Wat Plai Laem? | In Thai tradition the big smiling figure is Phra Sangkachai, a wise disciple of the Buddha, often confused with Budai, the Chinese Happy Buddha.
How long should I spend at Wat Plai Laem? | Most visitors need 30–45 minutes; add about an hour if you also visit Big Buddha.
Is Wat Plai Laem good for children? | Yes, children usually enjoy feeding the fish, but hold small hands near the platform edges, where railings are low.
